subject.title: fix(infra): fix exec-approvals async lock, not just the sync path (#106777, extends #108971)

question: Should exec approvals intentionally maintain a local asynchronous sidecar-lock implementation rather than fixing or extending the shared file-lock dependency?
rationale: The affected file governs authorization state for tool execution, and the choice determines the long-term owner of stale-lock, contention, and recovery semantics beyond this one VirtioFS failure.

options.title: Own the local authorization lock
options.body: Accept the local nonce lock after proving its fail-closed and cross-process behavior matches the required exec-approval contract.

options.title: Repair the shared lock upstream
options.body: Move the nonce ownership repair into the shared locking dependency and keep exec approvals on the common implementation.

options.title: Pause for a narrower contract review
options.body: Hold this PR until an owner defines whether auth-state locking may intentionally diverge from other file-lock consumers.

recommendation.title: Own the local authorization lock
recommendation.body: Accept the local nonce lock after proving its fail-closed and cross-process behavior matches the required exec-approval contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identified author of the predecessor nonce-based lock design that this PR extends.
